review_reference: UNSIGNED: reviewed_by stays empty until the owner signs. Release A integration (coordinator's hand-over of 18 November 2026 on hid-system#258; Rahman integration owner, DB). One owner signature for 0128-0137: 0128 (#264), 0129 (#266), 0130 and 0131 (#272), 0132 (#273), 0133 and 0134 (#280, Ola), 0135 (#274), 0136 (#275), 0137 (#276). Owner decisions followed: Q100 B, Q101, Q102, Q103 A, Q104, Q105, Q106, Q108 A, Q109 (also: no daily limit on registration without a NIN, coordinator 19 November), Q110, Q111 A, Q112 A, Q113 A, Q115 A as changed (19 November), and ORD-2. Q120 B, Q121 A and Q122 A (19 November) are built into 0133 as taken from Ola's #280 at 7bb3e112 (her final fingerprint, posted on hid-system#258 at 22:00 UTC); Q119 (several outside pharmacies sharing one prescription's quantity) and Q123 A (work lists of open work plus the last 90 days) come after Release A. Releases after 0124-0127 (live); production's pending set is then exactly the files below.
evidence: Each file's suite, the full database suites and the PG16 upgrade rehearsal on throwaway clusters with fictional data only, as posted on hid-system#258 with the sha256 of each file. 0128: the PIN-use inbox notice naming the clinician, role and facility; the access-request list names the requester. 0129: a staff member's chosen facility kept per sign-in (behind STAFF_FACILITY_SELECTION_MODE, off by default). 0130: front-desk registration without a NIN (phone required except for a child; the desk creates the record with no possible duplicate, otherwise an approver who did not start it decides); no daily limit (Q109), the facility's count today only for an operations alert. 0131: doctors, nurses and clinicians open their own facility's patient for 24 hours without a PIN (registered here or a consented visit here in 24 months), shown in the patient's access history and revocable by the patient. 0132: staff patient search (strong keys everywhere, weak keys own facility only) and emergency search by exact names and date of birth (break-glass holders, a reason, shown in the patient's access log); cards carry a 10-minute matchRef, never a Health ID or patient id; break-glass by an emergency card's matchRef (ID-5) runs 0031's activation unchanged for that patient, and an unresolved ref is refused as an unknown Health ID. 0133 (ORD-2): this facility's pharmacist and lab scientist work on its own prescriptions and lab requests without a consent grant (the work items and their chain only, never the chart; a patient's deny directive still applies), and an activated prescription goes automatically to the hospital's own pharmacy when it is staffed; a hold or an edit withdraws the send and the prescriber is told; only a session that sets app.own_facility_work to '0133' (the new lab-api and pharmacy-api images, in every staff transaction) gets this access, so today's images see what they see on 0001-0127 and either image can be rolled back alone (Q120 B). Q121 A (D14): until the hospital's own pharmacy has dispensed a prescription, the new ehr-api may send it to an outside pharmacy under today's order-route rule, and the own item is then withdrawn as sent elsewhere (it leaves the pharmacy's list, and the database refuses its dispensing for every image: 23514, DETAIL sent_elsewhere); one unique index (one own and one route-backed item per prescription) replaces 0023's two keys, and an owner-only claims table keeps at most one live claim per prescription, so nothing is dispensed twice; ehr.send_order_route and ehr.order_route_resend_allowed answer as 0123 and 0086 do for any session without the switch. Q122 A (D15): an owner-only list of the patients with own work per kind and facility, kept by triggers; the row's half is split per kind (the Pharmacy runtime's and the Lab runtime's, neither for the other) and answers only for a patient on its own kind's list at that facility. Rollout: pharmacy-api with or before ehr-api. Undo: restore 0123's send and 0086's resend flag first; the claims table, its triggers and the key change are never dropped; 0133's header gives the order. 0133's own evidence in full (proofs at bfe1f18d, whose SQL equals 7bb3e112's; mutations; cost; eleven review rounds) is #280's draft declaration at 7bb3e112, which this combined declaration replaces. 0134 (Q102): a fictional pharmacist and lab scientist at the sealed QA tenant's QA Hospital, sealed QA only. 0135: the waiting list (check-in by matchRef or own-facility patient, stage, triage, assignee; no clinical content; not a visit). 0136: the role-table changes of Q103 A with Q111 A and Q112 A; stops at apply, changing nothing, if any real (non-sealed) staff would be affected (Q113 A). 0137: QoreID asked once per NIN, its stored answer and its hold; a record for a NIN not yet on a Health ID kept 90 days from the first check and at least 30 days from each later use, whichever is later (Q115 A as changed: one rule, applied by begin to every stored record it answers and by keep_qoreid_nin_record for the desk's matched record), a NIN-only record a sign-up cannot use answered from storage, and QoreID's not found for every check. LOCKS: every file that changes or references an existing table takes those tables first, NOWAIT, at the strongest mode it takes (measured with pg_locks before commit): retried every 100 ms for at most 5 seconds, else 55P03 with nothing applied; inside the runner's dry run, where the transaction already holds the earlier files' locks, one attempt and no sleep (0129 and 0133 as Ola wrote them; 0130, 0131, 0132, 0135 and 0136 since 19 November). NOWAIT covers table locks only; two waits remain, each bounded by the runner's 5 s lock_timeout. First, index locks behind a concurrent REINDEX (0133 takes auth.accounts' indexes NOWAIT by planning under a 10 ms lock_timeout; the other files do not). Second, 0136's step 4 behind a pending identity.access_requests row that a patient's approve or deny holds FOR UPDATE (0072): only a pending records-processing request by a staff member who loses ocr.job.write in 0136 (laboratory staff) can be such a row, and on live, with no real staff active (Q113 A), only a sealed QA one; if the approval's UPDATE then waits for 0136's table lock, PostgreSQL ends one of the pair (40P01): the approval answers an error and can be retried, or 0136 stops with nothing of it applied and is run again. In the dry run any such wait holds the earlier files' locks meanwhile, so the dry run belongs in a quiet window. 0128 is the first file, so it holds nothing when it starts. FILE BY FILE: the runner applies each pending file in its own transaction; the rehearsal proves today's live images (staging da84d595's service code, live since 19 November 16:20 UTC; staging 092cd248 changes no service code) pass their runtime verifiers on the schema left after 0132 and after 0135 (not after 0136, which changes the role table on purpose, Q103 A). Every file is additive or replaces bodies it pins by md5; runtime-grants.sql grants exactly what the files grant. INTEGRATOR CHECKS (19 November): no file but 0133 names lab.work_item_allows, pharmacy.work_item_allows, lab.work_items, pharmacy.work_items, ehr.prescriptions, ehr.send_order_route, ehr.order_route_resend_allowed or identity.own_work_patients, so none replaces what 0133 relies on or locks its tables; 0136 is 66e17d50.
